We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: step 1: sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). So retrosynthesis: break sulfonamide to sulfonyl chloride + aniline.

Target has sulfonamide linking a tolyl amine (para-methyl phenyl) to a sulfonyl phenyl bearing an α,β-unsaturated amide side chain.

So retrosynthetic disconnections:

1) Disconnection of sulfonamide: produce sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2-Cl) and aniline (Ar-NH2). The sulfonyl chloride would be the sulfonyl phenyl with the side chain attached? Actually the sulfonyl phenyl is attached to the side chain via the aromatic ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). The sulfonyl group attached to that phenyl ring. So sulfonyl chloride precursor: Cl-SO2-Ph- (the phenyl bearing the side chain). The amine precursor: p-toluidine (4-methyl aniline). So step 1: sulfonamide formation.

2) The side chain on the sulfonyl phenyl is an α,β-unsaturated amide: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2 (actually amide attached to aniline). The side chain could be formed via Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid, then amide formation with aniline (aniline is the second amine). So retrosynthesis:

Disconnection of the C=C double bond: break to aldehyde (aryl aldehyde) and malonic acid (or its derivative). The aldehyde would be the phenyl ring bearing the sulfonyl group? Actually the α,β-unsaturated acid is attached to the phenyl ring at para position? The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to sulfonyl. So the phenyl ring (c2) has a para substituent of the α,β-unsaturated amide. So the aldehyde precursor would be the same phenyl ring with a formyl group at that position (para-aldehyde). So we need p-sulfonyl phenyl aldehyde (i.e., 4-formyl phenyl sulfone). So step 2: Doebner modification to form the α,β-unsaturated acid from aldehyde + malonic acid.

3) Then amide formation: convert the carboxylic acid to amide with aniline (c3ccccc3N). So step 3: amide coupling.

Thus three steps: (retro) 1) sulfonamide cleavage, 2) amide bond cleavage, 3) Doebner modification cleavage (C=C formation). Actually order in forward: first Doebner to make unsaturated acid, then amide coupling, then sulfonamide formation. In retrosynthesis we reverse: start from target, first break sulfonamide, then break amide, then break C=C to aldehyde + malonic acid.

We need to produce JSON route with three reaction nodes.

We need template IDs for each transformation. We have some template IDs from earlier search: template 733 is sulfonamide formation (retro: sulfonamide -> sulfonyl chloride + aniline). That seems appropriate.

For amide formation (carboxylic acid to amide) we need a template. Search for amide formation? Let's search for template that breaks amide to acid + amine. Use functional_groups_broken: amide, formed: carboxylic acid and primary amine? Actually forward amide formation breaks carboxylic acid O-H and forms amide. Retro would break amide to acid + amine. So functional_groups_broken: amide, functional_groups_formed: aliphatic carboxylic acid, primary amines. Let's search.
